section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the praise of Yehudah requires the preparatory service of Reuven, Shimon, and Levi to reveal the constant, innate gratitude within every Jew.
section.t: Now, this quality of Yehudah requires the preparatory service of the aspects of Reuven, Shimon, and Levi,
meaning, in order that the gratitude of the aspect of Yehudah will be in revelation.
But in concealment and inwardness, this gratitude is constant.
And as explained in Torah Ohr23
that the yud of Yehudah indicates the present and constant, like "Thus did Iyov all the days"24,
meaning that the gratitude within each and every Jew is constant.
For what is written3
"This time I will thank Hashem"
(since not all times are equal)
applies only regarding revelation,
due to the concealment and hiding of the body and the Nefesh HaBahamis
(and especially due to the concealment and hiding of the exile),
but the Nefesh HaElokis within each and every Jew
[which is his true essence]
is always faithful with Him25
and "I will thank Hashem" is within him constantly,
and no change applies to this, G-d forbid.
And the preparatory service of the aspects of Reuven, Shimon, and Levi is in order to arouse26
the gratitude that is in the innerness of the heart so that it will be in revelation,
and until its effect emerges from potential to actual, in thought, speech, and action.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section discusses how the revelation of Yehudah's gratitude leads to "Your hand on the neck of your enemies" spiritually and physically, preceding the Messianic era.
section.t: And the verse continues, "Your hand on the neck of your enemies,"
that through the revelation of the gratitude of the aspect of Yehudah, "Your hand on the neck of your enemies" is achieved spiritually
(as the concept is explained in Torah Ohr27)
and also physically,
for a verse does not depart from its simple meaning28.
And after "Your hand on the neck of your enemies," it is stated, "A lion cub is Yehudah... the scepter shall not depart from Yehudah..."29,
and it can be said, as a possibility, that this hints that "Your hand on the neck of your enemies" is before the redemption30.
For, behold, "A lion cub... the scepter shall not depart from Yehudah" refers to Dovid and Shlomo,
from whose seed will be King Moshiach31
about whom it is said, "and a staff shall arise from Israel"32
[for then it will be, "And My servant Dovid shall be king over them"33,
and "Dovid My servant shall be their prince forever"34,
as stated in the haftarah of this past Shabbos,
"the eighth, all the days are blessed"35].
And before this,
at the conclusion of the time of exile36,
there will be "Your hand on the neck of your enemies,"
that all the enemies of Israel
[for all of Israel are called by the name Yehudah37]
will have dread and fear fall upon them38.
Through the revelation of the gratitude within the collective souls of Israel,
and until it comes into actuality in thought, speech, and action,
"If you walk in My statutes and keep My commandments..."39,
behold, through this there will be
(as the continuation of the verses in Parshat Bechukotai40)
"and your enemies shall fall before you..."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section connects Yehudah's praise to "Vayechi Yaakov in Egypt," explaining that Torah study in exile brings life and causes the nations to assist Israel, hastening the redemption.
section.t: And it can be said that this is also the connection of "Yehudah, your brothers shall praise you, your hand on the neck of your enemies" to "Vayechi Yaakov in the land of Egypt,"
that even when Israel is in exile
(for all exiles,
the kingdoms41
are called by that name)
Egypt is in the aspect of "Vayechi" through the study of Torah, the Torah of life, and the fulfillment of its commandments, about which it is said42
"and live by them"
[and according to the explanation of the Alter Rebbe, who said to his grandson, the Tzemach Tzedek, on the verse "Vayechi Yaakov in the land of Egypt,"
that through "Yehudah he sent before him... to instruct before him in Goshen, to prepare for him a house of study, etc."43
there was the aspect of "Vayechi" even in Egypt44],
and through this is achieved45
(Yehudah, your brothers shall praise you)
"Your hand on the neck of your enemies,"
and as our sages said46
when the voice is the voice of Yaakov in synagogues and study halls, the hands of Esav do not prevail,
and moreover,
the nations of the world themselves assist Israel in all material matters so that they can study Torah and fulfill mitzvos with ease,
and in a manner of increasing and adding light.
And this light pushes away the darkness of exile and brings the redemption through Moshiach Tzidkeinu,
may he come and redeem us and lead us upright to our land,
speedily in our days, literally.
